passage:
For Earth Day, a school displayed a large sign: "We do not inherit Earth from the past. We borrow it from the future."
Students discussed what the sentence meant. One said it meant children in the future would live with the results of today's choices. Another said it made adults sound like temporary guests.
The class then examined their school's waste, electricity use, and green spaces. They chose one project: reducing single-use lunch items.
The sentence did not give technical instructions, but it changed the way students thought.
A powerful idea can make a familiar place feel like a responsibility. The school was not just theirs. It also belonged to people not yet born.
